correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary slice functional, the dual-coordinate norms \(b_\gamma\) produce \(c_\gamma=b_\gamma^{q-1}\in S_{\ell_p}\). Coordinate Daugavet witnesses give a point in the same slice with distance approaching \(\|a+c\|_p\). The scalar infimum is exact because \(F(t)=(1+t)^p-t^p\) is increasing and coordinate unit vectors approach the infimal coordinate norm. A coordinate-supported slice supplies the matching upper bound. Zero coordinates, unattained infima, singleton families and arbitrary index cardinality are handled by the argument.
risks: The proof is for real spaces and \(1<p<\infty\); endpoints and complex scalars are outside scope.

value.rationale: The result computes a recently introduced localized invariant on a natural direct-sum class, identifies the exact finite-sum control parameter, and shows an infinite-index collapse to a flat unit-sphere profile. It is structural information not recoverable from the known global thickness constant and is not a small-instance computation.
risks: Its novelty remains literature-search based, with terminology mismatch the main residual risk.

limitations: Real Banach spaces and \(1<p<\infty\) only; no endpoint, complex-scalar, non-Daugavet, or Delta-constant extension.
